cases.name: python_repl
cases.label: python_repl
cases.description: Execute Python code in a persistent Python REPL. Top-level `await` is supported. Variables, imports, and loaded data persist across calls, and are revived on a best-effort basis when a session is resumed (objects that cannot be serialized are dropped and reported). `cancel_background: true` stops a backgrounded cell that holds the kernel in synchronous code before this cell runs; a cell that ignores the cancel's interrupt has its kernel retired. Run shell commands with `bash('cmd')` / `await bash('cmd')`. Project imports, tests, scripts, CLIs, and dependency checks should run through the target project's own environment.
cases.promptSnippet: python_repl - persistent Python REPL for code, state, and bash() orchestration

code.description: Python code to execute in the persistent Python REPL. Use the target project's own environment for project imports, tests, scripts, CLIs, and dependency checks instead of direct kernel imports.

timeout.description: Seconds this call waits before auto-backgrounding a still-running cell (default 60 unless the user configured otherwise, max 180). The cell keeps running and its completion notice arrives in the inbox, or as a full session row when it carries rich output.

cancel_background.description: Stop the session's backgrounded Python cell before running this cell. Use it when an earlier cell auto-backgrounded and now holds the kernel in synchronous code (the KernelBusy refusal names that cell): the cell is interrupted, and a cell that ignores the interrupt has its kernel retired, losing unsnapshotted state. The result says whether a cell was stopped.
